en: The pleasure of love lasts only a moment,
the sorrow of love lasts all one's life.
I gave up everything for ungrateful Sylvie;
she leaves me and takes another lover.
The pleasure of love lasts only a moment,
the sorrow of love lasts all one's life.
"As long as this water flows gently
toward the stream that borders the meadow,
I will love you," Sylvie kept telling me…
The water still flows, yet she has changed!
The pleasure of love lasts only a moment,
the sorrow of love lasts all one's life.
notes: The English follows the site owner's own translation, fitted to the lines as printed.
The poem is a song in Florian's novella Célestine (1784).
